title: Azoth Keycard
description: The file a user supplies to extend or override what this library ships: components, fluids, fittings, coefficients, and declarative model definitions. It is the way to add to azoth without writing Rust or Python - a component, a fluid, a coefficient and a cubic variant are all data. **Every section belongs to one of two stages, declared as `x-azoth-stage` on the section itself.** A `runtime` section is read by the loaded keycard at the moment a calculation is called, so a change takes effect immediately. A `compiled` section is consumed by a generator that writes a shipped data file, so a change takes effect after a regeneration and a rebuild. Nothing in the format says which; a reader has to be told, which is what the annotation is for. **A keycard is the user's, and this library does not police it.** A row may carry a citation; nothing requires one and nothing validates one. The engineer supplying data is responsible for its provenance and for their right to use it, which is a professional responsibility no schema can discharge.

schema_version.description: The keycard format's version. Version 2 added `components`, `coefficients` and `models`. Bumped rather than extended in place because the checker that reads version 1 does not reject unknown sections - so a version-1 file carrying `components` would be accepted and the section silently dropped, which is data that looks in use and is read by nothing.

keyholder.description: Who is asserting the right to use these values. Optional, and nothing in azoth reads it: no result carries it and no check requires it. It is here so that a keycard says whose it is.

name.description: The person or organisation holding the licence, as they want to be named.

licence.description: A fetchable reference to the licence itself, so a reviewer can see the terms a value was used under rather than being told they exist. Optional: a keycard carrying only public data has no licence to name.

fluids.description: Property tables, keyed by fluid name, overriding or extending `data/fluids/`.

components.description: A component databank, keyed by substance name. A component is a *set* of named parameters rather than a fixed record, because the models need different ones - a cubic needs `Tc`, `Pc` and `omega`, an associating model needs those plus association parameters - so the parameter names are open and the checker refuses one no model reads. Supplying a name the shipped databank already has overrides it; supplying a new one extends it.

kij.description: Binary interaction parameters, overriding or extending `data/components/kij.csv`. An array of rows rather than a map, because the key is a *pair* and every spelling of one - `a|b`, `b,a`, nested objects - is a convention nobody can guess. These are the values a cubic's mixing rule actually reads, so a keycard that overrides a component's `Tc` but not its interaction parameters is overriding less than it looks like.

temperature_k.description: The temperature the parameter was fitted at, where the source says. Optional: most published `kij` are treated as constants, and recording a temperature where the source gives one is disclosure, not a requirement.

coefficients.description: Single constants a calculation takes as an argument, keyed by calculation id and then by input name - the identifiers the spec, both implementations and the registry already use. These are a *default*: a caller who passes the argument explicitly wins and the keycard is not consulted.

unit.description: Required, and checked against the spec's declared unit for that input. It is the one silent-error risk the entry carries: a coefficient declared in the wrong unit is a factor with no symptom.

convention.description: Which convention the value is stated in, where the quantity is not a true ratio. `control_valve_cv`'s `Cv` is the case: it is declared `dimensionless` because no vocabulary unit can express `gpm/sqrt(psi)`, and that declaration is a fiction the warning carries instead.

models.description: Declarative model definitions. A restricted, data-only form: named choices from closed vocabularies plus numeric parameters, with nothing to execute. Both implementations interpret the form independently and are cross-checked, which is what keeps the two-implementation guarantee true for a model this repository cannot see.

kind.description: The model family. **One member, and deliberately.** A kind is here only when both implementations run it and a contract test holds the vocabulary to them together - the argument `docs/src/theory/solvers.md` already makes about `solver.kind`. Widening this enum is a deliberate act that happens alongside the implementation, never before it.

shape.description: Named as a pair rather than as loose numbers because it fixes the cubic's two constants (`e`, `f`), and naming them separately would make an invalid combination representable. **One member, and deliberately** - the same rule `kind` states above: a shape is here only when both implementations run it and a contract test holds the vocabulary to them together. An earlier draft listed five cubics and six alpha functions, none of which the code implemented; a keycard declaring one would have been accepted, stored, and silently evaluated as Peng-Robinson. Widening an enum is a deliberate act that happens alongside the implementation, never before it.

alpha.description: One member for the same reason as `shape`. See `eos.pr_kappa` and `eos.pr_alpha_ab`: the alpha function is `[1 + kappa(1 - sqrt(Tr))]**2` with `kappa = 0.37464 + 1.54226*omega - 0.26992*omega**2`. Mathias-Copeman and Twu are fitted forms with their own parameters; nothing here reads `alpha_parameters`, so declaring one would be a promise this build cannot keep.

mixing_rule.description: One member: van der Waals one-fluid mixing with binary interaction parameters, which is what `eos.vdw1f_mix_binary` implements and what the flashes mix with. A keycard's `kij` rows are the parameters this rule reads.

components.description: Component names, resolved against this keycard's `components` section.

alpha_parameters.description: The extra parameters an alpha function needs. Present and empty for the one this build implements, which needs none - and left in the format because it is how a fitted alpha function would arrive. The `if/then` branches that required `eta` for Mathias-Copeman and `L`, `M`, `N` for Twu are gone with those members: a constraint on a value the enum no longer admits is a rule that can never fire.
